Ballotpedia's roundup lists him among the Senate sponsors of HB 1334 (absentee voting). As introduced, it required absentee ballot applications to ask for a driver's license number, ID card number, or voter registration number plus the last four digits of the Social Security number. Secondary source; the official bill page could not be read.

findings.passage: Bill sponsor Sen. Eric Koch, a Republican from Bedford, said he believes Indiana’s elections are “safe and secure” but cited scattered criminal cases of absentee voting fraud from across the state over the past decade.
findings.note: Reporter's sentence; only the words "safe and secure" are his direct quote, the rest is the reporter's summary of what he said when the Senate voted 36-12 for HB 1334, which asks for a photocopy of ID or two ID numbers with a paper mail-ballot application.
